mechanisms.decisive_claim: For every prime b and all sufficiently large K, with m=floor(K/16), there is a support-minimal bad path relation of 2m+1 distinct P_K-coprime integers in (b^K/b^19,b^K], uniformly for controlled primes below b^m and different from b.
mechanisms.kill_test: Derive exact Bertrand, ceiling-error, decrement, nonnegativity, distinctness, and support-minimality inequalities for every sufficiently large K.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same fixed-width theorem follows with s=floor(K/2) and tail constant b^4 using repeated Bertrand intervals alone.
mechanisms.kill_test: Apply the worst-case Bertrand bound to the largest product of two edge primes and compare its base-b exponent with K.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The path relation can be padded so that every vertex has the same valuation at the padding prime b, making the full controlled signature identical even when b is observed.
mechanisms.kill_test: Sum the b-valuations on the two unequal shores under the assumption that every vertex has one common value.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A connected regular bipartite edge-prime graph can have unequal part sizes and gives a locally indistinguishable support-minimal bad relation.
mechanisms.kill_test: Equate the number of edges counted from the two parts of a positive-degree regular bipartite graph.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The zero controlled-valuation fibre can be used even when the padding prime b belongs to the controlled set.
mechanisms.kill_test: Inspect the positive b-adic padding exponents of the constructed vertices and compare with the zero signature.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For every growing controlled-prime set below b^m, any o(N) union of valuation fibres must retain the all-zero fibre.
mechanisms.kill_test: Take increasingly many small primes and test whether the count of integers avoiding all of them remains a positive fraction of N.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: If sum over controlled primes of 1/p is at most 1-delta, then every o(N) lower-threshold plus complete valuation-cylinder deletion misses a support-minimal bad relation for N=b^K along all sufficiently large K.
mechanisms.kill_test: Prove a delta N lower bound for the zero fibre, force that fibre to be retained, and place every constructed vertex above the o(N) cutoff with zero signature.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: One constant-width path relation refutes every adaptive local or residue-aware owner rule with o(N) total deletion cost.
mechanisms.kill_test: Allow the rule to select one distinguished vertex of this single relation and check whether any global lower bound follows.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For independent deletion with q_K(n)<=g_K log(N/n)/log N and g_K=o(log N), no unaltered sample is a transversal almost surely for every sufficiently large N.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use the constant-width path to bound all q_K(n)<1 and show its vertices jointly survive with strictly positive probability.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The logarithmic support size of one constant-width minimal relation implies tau(H_N) is at least a positive multiple of log N.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute the hitting number of a hypergraph containing only the displayed edge and determine what additional packing would be required.
